A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V2 reports original GDP-based simulations measuring coverage, confidence-interval widths, and power in Section 5 and Appendix 7.1, plus runtime experiments in Appendix 7.8.

after.justification: V3 retains the original GDP-based simulation results in Section 5 and Appendix A.1, with runtime experiments presented in Section 5.2.

M1.justification: The variance-maximizing integer program, marginal constraints, extensions to linear- and quadratic-in-treatment estimators, and Algorithm 1 bootstrap procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use 2017–2019 IMF GDP data for the same geographical simulations, including null, additive, and multiplicative effects under complete randomization and matched pairs. V3's explicit 50-country restriction in the dataset paragraph repeats information already in v2's scalability paragraph.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain the same comparisons against Sampling Boot., Conservative Var., and Isotone Copula. Comparator participation and the omitted matched-pairs isotone results are unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the same sample selection, balanced treatment allocation, matching by 2018 GDP, pre-period adjustment, estimators, and coverage, interval-width, and power metrics. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The null-effect scalability analysis moves from Appendix 7.8 to Section 5.2 without changing its evidence. Covariate comparisons and the four-unit undercoverage example in Appendix 7.11/A.10 are also retained.

E5.justification: Both already report 10 simulation runs per runtime data point and 95% confidence intervals based on standard errors. The bootstrap resampling counts and uncertainty-reporting procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 match, and Figures 1–2 contain identical runtime plots. For example, Table 1 retains optimal causal bootstrap interval widths of 3348 and 2233 without covariates under complete randomization and matched pairs, respectively.

T1.justification: The feasibility lemma, validity bounds, assumptions, and appendix proofs and derivations are retained. Theorem renumbering and mathematical display changes do not revise the theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same generalization scope, asymptotic-validity claims, and claims about refined confidence intervals for geographical experiments. The abstract's duplicated-word correction does not change these contributions.

C2.justification: Explanations of heavy-tail undercoverage, matched-pairs isotone failure, and covariate effects remain unchanged, as do computational and applicability limitations. The added generic impact statement introduces no substantive scientific qualification.

D1.justification: Appendix 7.1/A.1 retains the CP-SAT solver link, 100 cloud CPU workers, and approximately two hours of experiment runtime. Data access information and the disclosed integer versus linear programming implementations are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained, including relationships to Aronow et al. (2014) and Imbens and Menzel (2021). Citation formatting, reference ordering, and minor bibliographic metadata changes do not alter that positioning.

P1.justification: V3 makes limited wording edits, adds an impact statement and acknowledgments, and divides Section 5 into Empirical Results and Scalability Analysis. It consolidates existing scalability material and states the sample restriction earlier; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 substantially reformats the main text and references into a two-column conference layout with different typography, headers, and display spacing. Figures 1–2 move from separate appendix pages to side-by-side main-text placement; Tables 1–2 are grouped on one page with expanded design labels.

improvement.justification: V3 makes practical scope and computational cost easier to assess by stating the 50-country sample in the dataset paragraph and consolidating previously separated runtime discussion and plots in Section 5.2. These are modest organizational gains; the methods, theory, empirical evidence, and substantive qualifications are unchanged.
